project_name: San Mateo 230/115 kV Transformer Bank Addition Project
load_growth_evidence: Report states overloads worsen from 20% in 2026 to 38% in 2034, driven by 'distribution customers in San Francisco and the Peninsula, the increasing demand for electric vehicle (EV) charging, electrification loads, and the interconnection of large customer loads.' AATE and AAFS loads will further increase overloads beyond 2034.
objectives: • To eliminate overloads on San Mateo banks f or P6 contingencies
alternatives_rejected: • BESS. Not recommended due to insufficient capacity in the charging window. • Power Flow Control Device. Not recommended due to the multiple power f low controllers required • RAS. Not applicable per ISO RAS Guidelines where involuntary load tripping is not allowed in high density load areas
driver_detail: Category P6 contingency overloads on the remaining transformer when two of three 230/115 kV banks at San Mateo are lost. Overloads worsen progressively: 20% in 2026, 23% in 2029, 38% in 2034, and 'forecasted AATE and AAFS loads will further increase these overloads beyond 2034.' The worsening trajectory driven by EV charging, electrification, and large customer load interconnections confirms load_growth. The P6 transformer loss scenario is the equip_aging trigger (insufficient transformer redundancy for current and future load).

P2 and P6 contingency overloads on six 115 kV lines/cables serving North Oakland; worst P6 case loads cables to 127.5–158.9% of summer emergency rating in 2034. The OCEI project (previously approved) is insufficient. Project rebuilds Sobrante-Grizzly-Claremont lines into four higher-capacity lines and adds GIS conversion at Oakland C (equip_aging).

load_growth_evidence: Report states: 'Significant load growth is anticipated at San Leandro, Edes, Oakland J, and Grant 115 kV Substations.' Data center load interconnection projects totaling more than 300 MW are actively being studied near East Shore substation.
objectives: To eliminate overloads on multiple 115 kV transmission lines in the Oakland South pocket under P1 to P7 contingencies and address the high growth demand in South Oakland.
alternatives_rejected: • New 230 kV source. Not recommended due to the limited load-serving capability on the 115 kV side • 115 kV topology changes. Not recommended as they do not eliminate the long-term need to reconductor most lines, making this solution cost-ineffective.
interim_solution: Oakland J and San Leandro RAS and operational solutions such as sectionalizing the South Oakland grid under P3 and P6 contingencies.
driver_detail: Explicit significant load growth: 'Significant load growth is anticipated at San Leandro, Edes, Oakland J, and Grant 115 kV Substations.' Additionally, 'data center load interconnection projects totaling more than 300 MW have been requested and are actively being studied near the East Shore 115 kV Substation.' P1–P7 contingency thermal violations on five primary 115 kV lines between Moraga and the South Oakland pocket. Reconductoring five 115 kV lines to at least 2288 Amps resolves the existing conductor capacity gap (equip_aging).

project_name: Greater Bay Area 500 kV Transmission Reinforcement
load_growth_evidence: LCR deficiency of nearly 5,000 MW in 2039 scenario. South Bay projected 2.5 GW load growth between 2026 and 2039. Report states: 'The anticipated increase in load significantly surpasses the available transmission resources and internal generation capacity.'
objectives: Reduce the LCR need in the Bay Area and address the high growth demand in the South Bay. • Prevent the overloads on the Panoche-Las Aguillas-Moss Landing 230 kV path • Increase the transmission capability between the South and North systems.
alternatives_rejected: • HVDC line f rom Warnerville to Newark. proved to be less ef f ective in alleviating the loading on the multiple overloaded lines and also showed minimal benef it in relieving congestion on the Panoche-Las Aguillas-Moss Landing 230 kV path • Tesla – Newark area new 500/230 kV station. Not recommended for the same reason described in above alternative May 30, 2025
driver_detail: Load_growth: 'Recent planning cycles have shown a significant increase in load demand, driven by factors such as transportation electrification, fuel substitution, and anticipated large load interconnections.' Long-term LCR deficiency of nearly 5,000 MW in the 2039 scenario; South Bay (San Jose/Silicon Valley) alone projected to grow by 2.5 GW between 2026 and 2039 (40% of total GBA growth). Economic: the project also relieves known congestion on the Panoche-Las Aguillas-Moss Landing 230 kV path, providing economic transmission benefits to the GBA system. Type is Reliability with economic objectives.

objectives: • To eliminate overloads on the Metcalf 500/230 kV transf ormer banks f or P6 contingencies

Demand is 'mainly driven by the distribution customers in the Silicon Valley area and newly interconnected large load, such as data centers and other related data-driven industries.' Equip_aging: three banks are insufficient transformer redundancy for the current and projected load. Load_growth: Silicon Valley data center-driven load is the explicit growth driver.

project_name: New San Jose B-NRS 230 kV line
load_growth_evidence: Long-term San Jose area load forecast increased from 2,100 MW in the 2021-2022 TPP to ~3,400 MW (base) and ~4,200 MW (sensitivity) in the 2024-2025 TPP—a 62-100% increase. The previously approved HVDC projects were re-scoped and this new line was added as a complement.
objectives: • To complement the scope changes that have been made to the San Jose area HVDC lines and provide f urther load serving capability in the area.
alternatives_rejected: • The alternative analysis was assessed in the San Jose area HVDC lines rescope assessment. Since this is a complementary component of the project, no alternatives were evaluated. May 30, 2025
driver_detail: The long-term load forecast in the San Jose area increased from 2,100 MW (2021-2022 TPP) to ~3,400 MW base / ~4,200 MW sensitivity scenario in the 2024-2025 TPP. The previously approved two San Jose HVDC projects were re-scoped due to this load increase. This new 230 kV line (San Jose B to SVP NRS, ~7 miles) complements the HVDC re-scope by providing an additional path for the 1,000 MW HVDC injection and a backup 230 kV source during DC supply outage. Driven entirely by dramatic long-term load growth in the San Jose area.

load_growth_evidence: Objectives explicitly cite 'the aggressive ramp-up in load trends reflected in the current load forecast.' South Bay hosts many AI/data-driven companies. Previously approved projects were re-scoped because load forecast significantly increased since their approval.
objectives: • To ensure enough transmission capacity and reliability in the South Bay to prevent the 115 kV system overloads due to the aggressive ramp-up in load trends ref lected in the current load f orecast • To reinf orce the most important 115 kV paths in the South Bay af ter the interconnection of the other bigger scope proposed projects for the area, such as the 500 kV line to Metcalf , the 500/230 kV transf ormer bank at this substation, the 1,000 HVDC line Metcalf – San Jose B, and the Newark – NRS, and NRS – San Jose B 230 kV lines.
alternatives_rejected: • Additional sources into the pocket or expansion of existing substation to prevent overloads. These type of alternatives are not recommended, since this need is already addressed by the bigger scope proposed projects for the area. • Given the high complexity of constructing new transmission assets or upgrading the existing grid in a densely populated urban environment, the lines identified for reconductoring do not have feasible alternatives for comparison. May 30, 2025
interim_solution: Operating solutions such as PST adjustment, HVDC ramp-down, and Los EsterosNortech-NRS 115 kV reactor switching
driver_detail: Explicit aggressive load growth: the report's objectives state 'the aggressive ramp-up in load trends reflected in the current load forecast' as the primary cause of thermal violations in the South Bay 115 kV network. Previously approved projects (San Jose HVDC lines, Metcalf-Piercy & Swift, Newark-Dixon Landing upgrade) are no longer sufficient due to load forecast increases. P1, P2, P3, P6 violations on 115 kV paths connecting Metcalf with San Jose B and Monta Vista with Ravenswood. Reconductoring seven 115 kV lines to 1400–3000 Amps addresses existing conductor undersizing (equip_aging).

project_name: Metcalf-Piercy & Swift and Newark-Dixon Landing 115 kV Upgrade (re-scope)
load_growth_evidence: Objectives explicitly state 'to prevent system overloads due to the aggressive ramp-up in load trends reflected in the current load forecast.' The project required re-scoping specifically because load forecast increases made the original reconductoring insufficient.
objectives: To ensure enough transmission capacity and reliability in one of the most importants 115 kV links between Newark and Metcalf to prevent system overloads due to the aggressive ramp-up in load trends reflected in the current load f orecast
driver_detail: Re-scope of a project originally approved in the 2003 TPP. Objectives explicitly state the cause: 'the aggressive ramp-up in load trends reflected in the current load forecast.' The San Jose area load forecast has increased dramatically since the original project approval, making the originally proposed 795 ACSS reconductoring insufficient. Re-scoped to use advanced conductors achieving 3,000+ Amps summer emergency rating on four lines (Piercy-Metcalf, Swift-Metcalf, Newark-Dixon Landing, McKee-Piercy). Equip_aging: existing line capacity is undersized for projected loads.
